# `orders`
Columns: id, customer, ordered_at, store_id, subtotal, tax_paid, order_total, order_weekday, order_hour
Measures: total_revenue, net_sales, tax_collected, order_count, unique_customers, avg_order_value, effective_tax_rate, sales_weighted_aov
Aggregations: dollars, weighted_avg
Joins to: customers, stores

SQL:
SELECT
  stores.name AS "orders.stores.name",
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN orders.ordered_at >= CAST('2024-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
      AND orders.ordered_at < CAST('2025-01-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP)
      THEN orders.subtotal
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) / 100.0 AS "orders.rev_2024_test",
  SUM(orders.subtotal) / 100.0 AS "orders.all"
FROM orders AS orders
LEFT JOIN stores AS stores
  ON orders.store_id = stores.id
GROUP BY
  stores.name
ORDER BY
  "orders.stores.name" ASC
LIMIT 50

args.message: San Francisco grew revenue fastest, by about 310% (growth of 3.098). "Revenue" here means sales before tax, in dollars. Los Angeles and New Orleans are left out because they had no sales in 2024. One caveat: San Francisco opened on 2024-07-07 and Chicago on 2024-06-27, so their 2024 figures cover only part of the year, which makes their growth look much bigger. Among the stores open for all of both years, Brooklyn grew fastest at about 6.8%, ahead of Philadelphia at about 3.9%.
